title: KitePay POC scoping - workload & benchmarks
summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling for KitePay's fraud-detection and reconciliation assistants. Discussed QPS, concurrency, input/output token distributions, target SLAs (p95 latency), cost targets, and proposed benchmark plan. Redwood AE+SE to run dedicated vs hosted perf comparison using production traces; finalized success criteria and timeline for a 2-week benchmarking POC starting Dec 7.
next_steps: Redwood: share benchmark plan and synthetic traffic config (Sana) - by 2026-12-04
KitePay: provide 1 week of anonymized production traces and 2000 sample prompts - by 2026-12-06
Schedule kickoff run for Dec 7 and baseline tests Dec 8-10 (AE + SE)
Follow-up check-in w/ results and pricing week of Dec 21
action_items: Sana Malik (Redwood SE): prepare benchmark config for dedicated vs hosted (A10/4xA100 configs) and traffic replay instructions - due 2026-12-04
Jordan Price (AE): send security documentation links (SOC2/ISO, KMS options) and pricing tiers - due 2026-12-04
Maya Chen (KitePay): export 7 days anonymized request traces + 2k sample prompts and redaction notes - due 2026-12-06
Ravi Kapoor (KitePay): provision test VPC endpoint and creds for private pilot if needed - target 2026-12-07
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Jordan Price (Redwood AE), Sana Malik (Redwood SE), Eli Ortega (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (KitePay Head of ML), Ravi Kapoor (KitePay Platform), Lena Ortiz (KitePay CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): discussing POC scope around throughput, latency targets, and modeling; agreement to run benchmark using anonymized traces and synthetic traffic; clarified success criteria for latency and cost.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for making time, can you hear me okay?
[00:04] Maya: yeah loud and clear, thanks Jordan.
[00:06] Lena: yep good.
[00:08] Jordan: cool quick intro — i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with me Sana and Eli who will run the bench and the tech bits. can you do a quick round from the kitepay side?
[00:18] Maya: sure im maya, head of ml. main use case is a realtime reconciliation assistant and a fraud signal enrichment callout. most calls are short but we have a small percent that are longer multi-step conversations when we ask for root cause.
[00:29] Ravi: ravi, platform eng, i'll handle creds and trace export.
[00:33] Lena: lena, cto, i'll be watching SLA/cost and security parts.

[00:40] Sana: great thanks. just to set expectations: we're scoping a POC focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling — QPS, concurrency, token distributions — and then we'll run a side-by-side benchmark hosted vs dedicated (and optionally private) to validate latency and cost.
[00:55] Maya: perfect. high level numbers from our side: avg qps right now 120 steady, we see peaks up to 550 during batch windows; concurrency usually around 40-90 during peaks. does that match what you normally see?
[01:08] Eli: that sounds very plausible. can you break down request sizes? short vs long?
[01:12] Maya: median input tokens 10-15, median output tokens around 30-45. about 12% of requests are long-form — 256-512 tokens outputs — mostly for investigation dialogs. 75% are short inference calls under 64 output tokens.
[01:29] Jordan: okay good. so to model this we'll want a distribution: 75% short (in/out <=64), 13% medium (65-256), 12% long (>256). also need your percentile latency requirements — what is acceptable p95/p99?
[01:45] Lena: for the realtime flows p95 should be <350ms ideally, p99 under 700ms. for the long investigative jobs we can accept p95 under 1.2s. cost targets are important too — want to keep unit cost predictable; we'll compare hosted vs dedicated to see delta.
[02:03] Sana: noted. for benchmarking we'll measure p50/p95/p99, tail jitter, and token throughput. we'll also profile KV cache warm vs cold. curious — do you use any caching at the app layer now?
[02:17] Maya: minimal. we tried some in-app cache but it's inconsistent because prompts vary. we could trial prefix caching if the runtime supports it.
[02:24] Eli: Redwood runtime has prefix/KV cache and automatic batching. We'll test with cache enabled and disabled to see delta. small note: transcription shows kv as 'k v' sometimes in our logs so there might be weird tokens, but we'll account for that.
[02:38] Ravi: for traffic modeling we can share 7 days of anonymized traces, including timestamps, model parameters, and lengths. can you tell us what format you need?
[02:46] Sana: csv or newline json works. each row: timestamp, prompt_type, input_tokens, output_tokens, latency_target (if available). that'll let us replay realistic arrival patterns (burstiness).
[02:56] Jordan: also we'd like 2k sample prompts for semantic quality checks so we can run output comparisons between models.
[03:03] Maya: we can do that.

[03:10] Jordan: benchmark plan proposal: run baseline on hosted (our standard) with your traffic replay for 48 hours, then dedicated reserved capacity (2x A10 / 4x A100 equivalent) and optionally a private VPC run if you want network isolation. measure QPS sustained, p95 latency for short flows, and cost per 1k tokens. does that timeline work?
[03:29] Lena: yes timeline wise budget allows 2 week window but we'd like initial results within first week.
[03:35] Sana: technically we'll do quick smoke tests day 1, run steady-state replay day 2-3, and longer mixed traffic with tail runs day 4-7. full comparatives and cost numbers by day 10-14.
[03:47] Eli: sample target configs: Hosted (standard service), Dedicated small (2xA10g equiv), Dedicated large (4xA100 equiv), with quantization variants where applicable. We'll include configs for batching and KV cache on/off.

[03:59] Ravi: question on concurrency modeling: our platform pushes to a job queue which then fanouts, so bursts are very bursty. can the replay mimic high-QPS spikes? we sometimes see 2-3x baseline for 30-60s windows.
[04:12] Sana: yes replay supports Poisson + burst overlay or exact timestamps. include both — we'll do exact timestamps from traces for fidelity and a synthetic burst test to stress tail.

[04:22] Maya: about quality — we need guardrails: for fraud enrichment, false positives are sensitive. how do we measure quality regression?
[04:28] Jordan: good question. success criteria will include qualitative checks: pass/fail thresholds on a small eval set (we'll run the 2k sample prompts and compare outputs against your current baseline with a small human review), plus latency/cost thresholds.
[04:41] Lena: concretely: success = p95 <350ms for 75% of traffic class, no >10% quality regression on eval set, and predictable cost delta within our budget (we'll supply budget numbers).
[04:54] Eli: note that model selection matters: different open models trade latency vs tokens generated. we'll include a couple of model variants in the bench — small fast model vs larger high-quality. quantized weights could cut latency/cost but sometimes affect quality; we'll measure delta.
[05:10] Maya: okay that helps. what's the expected QPS capacity for the dedicated small config?
[05:14] Sana: rough ballpark — 2x A10 could sustain ~200-300 qps for short-traffic with batching, 4x A100 could push 600-900 qps depending on token lengths and batching. we'll include realistic ranges in the plan.
[05:28] Ravi: curious about autoscaling behavior — during peaks do you recommend adding burst capacity or pre-warming?
[05:33] Jordan: for POC we'll model both. pre-warm + burst credits help with tail; dedicated pools can be configured for burst capacity. Also option to route non-critical long jobs to a lower-cost tier.

[05:45] Lena: security notes: we need SOC2 and ISO docs, and KMS integration details for private deployment. also audit logs retention.
[05:53] Jordan: i'll send links to SOC2 and KMS docs today. Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM and audit logs; we'll outline retention and access controls in the security pack.
[06:03] Maya: do you have any known limitations with our token distributions? eg cases where runtime slows dramatically?
[06:09] Eli: the typical slowdowns come from long KV cache misses and very long outputs >1k tokens. based on your 12% long-form, we expect manageable tails but we'll stress test to quantify.

[06:21] Ravi: for the POC can you run an A/B style run comparing hosted vs dedicated with identical request sequence?
[06:26] Sana: absolutely — we'll run identical replay sequences and produce per-request latencies and token counts so you can diff. we also produce aggregated charts (p50/p95/p99, token/s, cost breakdown).

[06:37] Jordan: quick bit on cost metrics we'll provide: cost per 1k input tokens, cost per 1k output tokens, compute-cost per hour for each config, and estimated monthly run rate at your projected qps.
[06:48] Lena: good. also is there a recommended way to estimate concurrency-to-latency mapping? our operations folks want a simple chart.
[06:56] Eli: yes we'll provide a concurrency vs p95 chart from the replay — basically run increasing concurrent workers and measure tail. that'll translate to number of instances to meet your p95 target.

[07:08] Maya: on timeline you said kickoff week of Dec 7. can we lock dates?
[07:12] Jordan: proposed schedule — Dec 7: kickoff & smoke; Dec 8-10 baseline hosted replay; Dec 11-14 dedicated runs & variants; Dec 15-18 private/VPC if needed; Dec 21 week: results + pricing review. does that align?
[07:25] Lena: yes that works, we'll aim to have traces by Dec 6.

[07:30] Ravi: a couple minor asks: please include example replay scripts and a small sandbox we can run internally to validate trace formatting.
[07:37] Sana: we'll include an example replay package and python scripts plus a small dockerized replay.

[07:42] Jordan: anything else on success criteria?
[07:45] Maya: can we add an uptime/availability target for the dedicated pool during tests? we'd like 99.9% during bench window and no more than 5% error rate.
[07:54] Eli: we'll aim for that during the POC and instrument error rates in reports.

[08:00] Jordan: great ok let's do a quick recap and next steps — Sana will share benchmark plan and replay repo by Dec 4, Jordan will send security docs and initial pricing, KitePay to send traces and sample prompts by Dec 6, and we'll start the POC on Dec 7. follow-up call to review results week of Dec 21.
[08:18] Lena: thanks all.
[08:20] Maya: thanks, looking forward.
[08:22] Jordan: thanks, we'll send notes. bye.

(There are occasional transcription artefacts: 'k v cache' sometimes transcribed as 'kay v cache', and speaker labels occasionally merged. Some proper nouns like A10G vs A10g may be mis-capitalized.)
